children: Delfi faces an earnings hit from elevated cocoa prices and currency headwinds, say UOB Kay Hian analysts in a research report. Although cocoa prices have retreated from 2024-2025 peaks, they remain historically elevated, with potential El Niño-related supply disruptions posing further risks, the analysts say. The Indonesian rupiah also depreciated 9.5% on-year in 3Q, weighing on sales from the chocolate confectionery products manufacturer's largest market and potentially lifting imported raw material costs. The brokerage cuts its 2026 and 2027 earnings forecasts for Delfi by around 5% each. It lowers the stock's target price to 0.88 Singapore dollar from S$0.98 with an unchanged buy rating. Shares are unchanged at S$0.635. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
